detail:
The Arthritis Foundation describes osteoarthritis management as a combination of approaches tailored to the joint involved, symptom severity, and overall health, rather than a single treatment. Sources describe regular physical activity, weight management when relevant, and physical therapy as foundations of day-to-day care. Therapists typically build programs around low-impact aerobic activity, strengthening for the muscles that support affected joints, and range-of-motion work, and occupational therapists may suggest assistive devices or joint-protection strategies for hand and other joint involvement.

The Arthritis Foundation notes that clinicians may discuss medicine classes such as analgesics, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), and, in selected cases, corticosteroid injections, weighing benefits against side effects and other health conditions. Heat and cold applications and supportive devices are also described as part of some care plans. For advanced disease with persistent pain and loss of function despite conservative care, clinicians sometimes discuss surgical options such as joint replacement, and sources present surgery as a later step rather than a first-line approach.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about managing osteoarthritis.
summary: The Arthritis Foundation describes osteoarthritis management built on physical activity, physical therapy, and weight management when relevant, with medicine classes and, for advanced disease, surgery discussed by clinicians in selected cases.
takeaways: activity and therapy are foundations sources describe for daily care
medicine classes are weighed by clinicians against other health conditions
never start, stop, or change medicines without your doctor
title: Osteoarthritis: managing joint pain and staying active day to day
